title: Everest would vanish into the deepest ocean with 2 km to spare
body: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, is the deepest known point of the seabed, nearly 11,000 m down. Drop Mount Everest (8,849 m) into it and its summit would still sit about 2 km below the waves. The water pressure at the bottom is more than 1,000 times that at the surface. The first people to reach it were Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh, in the bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960.

slides.prompt: Who were the first people to reach the bottom of the Challenger Deep, and when?
slides.answer: Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh, in 1960
slides.detail: They descended in the bathyscaphe Trieste, nearly 11,000 m down, where the water pressure is more than 1,000 times that at the surface.
